examples.metrics: Over 63% of highest-CTR videos highlight the key message within 3 s.

examples.name: Upworthy randomized headline tests (Robertson et al. 2023)
examples.what_works: Largest public record of A/B-tested hook language: negative stakes words raise clicks, positive words lower them; one honest stakes word in the hook is enough.
examples.metrics: ~105,000 headline variants, ~370 million impressions; +2.3% CTR per added negative word (average-length headline).

examples.name: Rockstar's GTA VI trailer rollouts (appointment plus countdown)
examples.what_works: Announcing reveal dates in advance turned trailers into appointments; when Trailer 1 leaked (Dec 2023) Rockstar released it early and said why, keeping the moment theirs. These are the anticipation mechanics a daily countdown borrows.
examples.metrics: Trailer 2: 475 million cross-platform views in 24 h per Rockstar (unverified this session).

recommendations: PACING SPEC (45-60 s): 135-180 spoken words at 180-190 wpm (~3 words/s, the reference's rate). First word by 0.2 s. Hook finished by ~2.5 s (6-9 words) in voice AND on-screen text. Sentences mostly 6-12 words (~3 s each), with 2-5 word staccato lines right after the rehook. First concrete number or list by 15-18% of runtime, midpoint rehook at 42-50%, payoff at 80-92%, CTA plus sign-off only in the last 2-4 s. No pause longer than ~0.3 s before the sign-off.

VISUAL RHYTHM WITH AI SHOTS (estimate): the reference averages one cut per ~6.2 s, about one generated clip. Generate ~10-12 shots per 55 s (one per beat, two for the mechanism beat), then use ffmpeg punch-ins, crops, speed ramps and number overlays so something on screen changes every 2-3 s. Frame 1 must already be moving. Save the strongest shot for the payoff. On the rehook line, make a hard visual break: new palette or angle plus a sound hit.

TOPIC AND HOOK SELECTION RULE: hook on things viewers already half-know (trailers, Vice City, the delays, preloading) and promise the part they don't (mechanism, number, history). Curiosity peaks at intermediate knowledge (Kang 2009) and needs a specific gap the reel can close (Loewenstein 1994). Never hook on rumors, datamines or leaked unreleased content. KILL LIST: greetings, logo stings, 'in this video', 'wait for it', fade-ins, context-first openers ('GTA 6 comes out on...').

HOOK TEMPLATE 1/10 - SECOND-PERSON PARADOX. Formula: 'You [already did/have X]. You [haven't/can't] [Y].' Example: 'You've probably watched GTA 6's second trailer more than once. You probably missed the line Rockstar put under it.' Why: people remember what relates to themselves (self-reference effect), plus a specific gap the reel can close. Frame 1: viewer-POV shot (controller, TV glow) + 3-5 word text. Guardrail: the 'you' statement must be true for most viewers; say 'probably' when it isn't universal.

HOOK TEMPLATE 2/10 - NUMBER FIRST. Formula: '[Exact number]. [What it counts].' then one perspective line. Example: '475 million views. In one day.' Why: surprise and awe drive attention and sharing (Berger & Milkman); the gap is 'of what?'; a human-scale perspective line helps the number land. Frame 1: the number full-screen, counting up. Guardrail: one number per hook, with an on-screen source tag in the same second.

HOOK TEMPLATE 3/10 - MYTH-FLIP. Formula: '[Common belief] isn't true. [Fact].' Example: 'GTA 6 isn't set in Vice City.' Why: contradicting an expectation sparks curiosity; negative framing raised clicks 2.3% per negative word in Upworthy's tests. Frame 1: the familiar image, then a hard zoom-out. Guardrail: flip only beliefs that are genuinely common, with a primary source in the caption.

HOOK TEMPLATE 4/10 - COUNTERFACTUAL CLOCK. Formula: 'If [official plan] had held, you'd [concrete consequence] by now.' Example: 'If Rockstar's first exact date had held, you'd be 170 days into GTA 6.' Why: second person + loss frame + exact number. Frame 1: calendar or counter rolling. Guardrail: recompute daily from the official dates and show both dates in the caption.

HOOK TEMPLATE 5/10 - IT HAPPENED BEFORE. Formula: '[Brand] has been burned by this before. In [year], [incident + number].' Example: 'Rockstar has been burned by leaks before. In 2022, about 90 clips of an unfinished GTA 6 got out.' Why: anxiety drives sharing; a year and a count signal fact, not rumor. Frame 1: dated case-file card. Guardrail: only adjudicated or officially confirmed incidents; never speculate about current leaks.

HOOK TEMPLATE 6/10 - WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS WHEN YOU... Formula: 'What actually happens when you [action the viewer takes this week]?' Example: 'What actually happens between pressing download and GTA 6 becoming playable?' Why: practical use + self-reference, strongest in launch week when everyone performs the action. Frame 1: macro shot of the button or progress bar. Guardrail: if the platform doesn't publish the mechanism, say so and label your explanation as the standard method, as the reference caption does.

HOOK TEMPLATE 7/10 - SCALE CONTRAST. Formula: '[Small or ordinary thing] vs [huge thing].' Example: 'Real Florida's highest point is a 345-foot hill. GTA 6 has a region called Mount Kalaga.' Why: awe from putting magnitudes side by side. Frame 1: split screen, small vs huge. Guardrail: both sides measurable and sourced.

HOOK TEMPLATE 8/10 - PAUSE CHALLENGE. Formula: 'Pause [official video] at [m:ss]. Look [exact spot].' Why: gives a reason to scrub and rewatch (replays count as views on Instagram and Shorts) and to comment 'found it'. Frame 1: freeze frame with a circle. Guardrail: verify the frame yourself and describe, don't speculate; the legal stream's footage-rights rules apply.

HOOK TEMPLATE 9/10 - WHY-QUESTION ON A KNOWN FACT. Formula: 'Why did [Rockstar/Sony/Microsoft] [known, verifiable action]?' Example: 'Why did Rockstar drop GTA 6's first trailer the night before its scheduled time?' (On-record answer: it had leaked; re-check Rockstar's Dec 2023 post.) Why: viewers know the what but not the why, and half-knowledge maximizes curiosity. Frame 1: the known moment with a question overlay. Guardrail: the answer must be on the record, not a theory.

HOOK TEMPLATE 10/10 - COUNTDOWN STAKES. Formula: 'In [N] days, [official, specific change] happens [to you / on millions of consoles]. Today: [one hidden part].' Example: 'In 7 days, GTA 6 unlocks on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Today: [topic].' Why: anticipation is itself enjoyable (Loewenstein 1987), effort rises as a goal nears (goal gradient), and it builds in a reason to follow. Frame 1: big T-N numeral, identical template every day. Guardrail: date only from Rockstar; switch to a count-up after launch.

SCRIPT TEMPLATE (hidden-side reel, 45-60 s): 10 beats in fixed proportions. Timings below are for 55 s (~165 words); use ~135 words for 45 s and ~180 for 60 s. To shorten, drop Beat 7 (or merge it into Beat 4) and give Beat 3 only one translation. Never cut the rehook, payoff or callback.

BEAT 1 HOOK (0-2.5 s, 6-9 words, 0-5%): one hook template, in second person or number first. On-screen text of 3-6 words says the same thing for sound-off viewers, placed in the upper-middle away from the bottom UI. Frame 1 is the most striking moving image, with the day numeral in a fixed corner. No logo, title card or greeting.

BEAT 2 STAKES + PROMISE (2.5-7 s, 12-15 words, 5-13%): why this matters to the viewer personally, and name the hidden part precisely so the gap is specific. Pattern: '[thing you know] has a part nobody talks about: [named mechanism].' Write it fresh each time.

BEAT 3 NUMBER SHOCK (7-15 s, ~24 words, 13-28%): say one number plainly, then restate it twice: once as a concrete unit (digits, gigabytes, days, views) and once as a human-scale comparison. Example from the reference: 340 undecillion keys, then 39 digits, then hundreds of universe ages. Show the number on screen as it is spoken. A short list (e.g., six region names) can stand in for the number.

BEAT 4 PROOF ON THE RECORD (15-23 s, ~24 words, 28-42%): one dated, sourced, real-world fact (a Rockstar statement, court finding or platform data, with place and date), plus a small on-screen source tag such as 'Rockstar, May 2025'. This is where trust is earned.

BEAT 5 MIDPOINT REHOOK (23-26 s, 6-8 words, 42-48%): a teaser line in your own words ('Now the detail most people miss.' / 'That's not the strange part.') with the hard visual break. Pay it off within 5 s or it reads as bait (Blom & Hansen 2015).
BEAT 6 MECHANISM (26-36 s, ~30 words, 48-66%): 4-6 staccato sentences of 2-7 words in a 'what you see vs what's actually happening' pattern. 2-3 quick cuts, with key terms labeled on screen.

BEAT 7 SECOND STAKES / HISTORY (36-44 s, ~24 words, 66-80%): 'This has gone wrong before. In [year], [specific incident + number]. [Consequence].' Year stamp on screen. Confirmed or adjudicated events only. Alternative: a second surprising number.

BEAT 8 PAYOFF = PEAK (44-50.5 s, 18-20 words, 80-92%): resolve the hook's paradox in one vivid before-and-after sentence anchored to launch ('On November 19, [before] becomes [after].'). Use the best shot of the reel here and peak the vocal energy (peak-end rule).

BEAT 9 CALLBACK + NEXT LOOP (50.5-53.5 s, 8-10 words, 92-97%): echo the hook's key word, then name tomorrow's topic precisely ('Tomorrow: why [specific].'). This is the reason to follow. On send-focused episodes, swap in one situational send line instead.

BEAT 10 SIGNATURE SIGN-OFF (53.5-55 s, 3-5 words, last 3%): your own fixed catchphrase plus the day marker (e.g., 'T-minus six.'). The last frame visually matches frame 1 and the audio tail is trimmed tight so the replay feels continuous.

CAPTION TEMPLATE: line 1 restates the hook's gap in different words; keep it short so it shows before 'more' (Instagram's cut-off length not verified this session). Then 2-3 lines extending the payoff. Then a RECEIPTS block with labeled lines: 'On the record:' (who, date), 'Reported:' (outlet, date), 'Our math:' (show the calculation), 'Estimate:' (what is assumed). Then one series line ('T-6 of [series name]: one verified piece of GTA 6 a day until Nov 19'), exactly one CTA, and 3-5 hashtags. Pin a comment repeating the source names.

CTA FOR SENDS (primary lever on a new account): one specific, situational send line after the payoff, max ~2 s, e.g., 'If someone you know is preloading tonight, send them this.' Avoid 'share this', 'tag 3 friends' or 'send to 10 people': Facebook has demoted share, tag and comment bait since 2017, and Instagram has no public rule either way. Make each reel worth sending: one awe number or one practical launch-night fact per reel.

CTA FOR FOLLOWS: never 'follow for more'. Tie the follow to a named next episode ('Tomorrow: why the trailer came straight out of a PS5.') and repeat the day marker on frame 1, in the sign-off and on the grid cover. Close today's gap completely and open a new one; a reel that holds back its payoff for 'part 2' invites 'clickbait' comments and fewer likes.

CTA COMMENT-KEYWORD DM (an inference from Mosseri's top-3 signals, untested): comments are not among the three signals Mosseri named, so treat keyword automations as list-building for later monetization, not reach. Use one only with a real deliverable (e.g., a sourced launch-week checklist), and put it in the caption and final 2 s, never the hook. Run it on at most 1 in 3 reels at first, and compare skip rate, average watch time and reach against reels without it before scaling. Use an official Meta-API tool such as ManyChat, never unofficial bots.

CTA FOR QUALITY COMMENTS: invite sourced corrections ('Spot an error? Drop the source.') or verifiable predictions about launch day. This builds the accuracy brand that makes the reels safe to send and keeps the no-rumor rule public.

ENDINGS THAT DRIVE REWATCHES: bookend, so the last spoken line echoes the first line's key word (reference: 'guarding' then 'guard it well'). The final frame matches frame 1 and the audio tail is trimmed for a seamless loop, since Instagram and YouTube Shorts both count replays as views. No outro card and no 'thanks for watching'. Optional: one dense frame worth pausing on (full 39-digit number, map with all six regions) shown for under 1 s.

SERIES DESIGN: count down from T-7 (Nov 12) to T-0 (Nov 19), then switch to a renamed count-up. Visible countdown numerals show progress toward the goal (Kivetz 2006). Keep a fixed daily posting time, the same frame-1 template with a big numeral, and the same sign-off. Each episode must stand alone for non-followers, with at most a one-clause recap. Pin a 'start here' reel and number the grid covers so profile visitors binge.

SERIES HORIZON: plan at least 8-10 weeks of daily posts past launch. Anticipation content loses its hook on launch day (Loewenstein 1987), and habits take a median of 66 days to form (Lally 2010). Post-launch 'hidden side' topics must be verified in your own gameplay or official sources, never datamines or rumors.

MEASUREMENT LOOP per reel: skip rate (hook and frame 1); retention at 3 s, at the rehook and at the payoff (Retention chart); average watch time; views per unique viewer (loop strength); sends per reach (shares / accounts reached, or native share rate if the April 2026 Insights update shows it); likes per reach; follows per reach. Diagnose: high skip rate = hook or frame 1; a cliff at 40-50% = weak rehook; a slide before the payoff = mechanism too long; good retention but few sends = payoff not worth sending. Change one variable at a time (same body, two hooks; Trial Reels if still available, unverified).

LENGTH TEST: 45-60 s is the right default for a new account's hook tests, but the reference holds 81 s at the same density. Once retention curves are stable, test one 70-80 s cut per week, since Instagram ranks on watch time. Prepare 61 s+ TikTok cuts if TikTok's Creator Rewards still requires videos over 1 minute (unverified).

ORIGINALITY GUARDRAILS: copy the structure, not the surface. Do not reuse the reference's gratitude opener, its 'guard it' framing, its 'unseen' or 'part you never see' wording, its sign-off, or its encryption/preload topic in the same week. Pick your own series name and catchphrase (ideas: countdown 'T-MINUS LEONIDA', then post-launch 'LEONIDA LOG'; check handle availability). Keep the labeled-receipts idea in your own labels.

VOICE DELIVERY: ~3 words/s, with energy rising into the payoff. End sentences on the key word ('...and nobody can play it') and use lists of three for rhythm. Faster speech is rated more credible and persuasive (Miller et al. 1976). Instant Voice Cloning copies the sample's delivery (unverified), so record the sample in reel style, not audiobook style.
